description: Found in defk-4ai. In out = alloc(i16, n); for i <- 0..(n - 1)//1 do out[i] = f(a[i], b[i]) end with n = min(len(a), len(b)), the reads of a and b are proven but the out[i] write keeps defk_put_* (a bounds branch that stops vectorisation): alloc/2 records only len_lo/len_lb (lower bounds of n relative to arrays), and min gives n no lower bound in terms of arrays. Natural shape for PCM mixing (defk-9p6.14) and other two-input elementwise kernels. Options: record that len(out) equals the C value of n (e.g. carry n's ub facts plus an identity fact so i <= n - 1 implies i < len(out)), or let loop variables carry ub facts relative to the alloc. Workaround today: out = alloc(e, len(a)) with i <- 0..(min(len(a), len(b)) - 1)//1. Done when: that kernel compiles with no bounds check in both reads and the write, test in both modes.
